articleTitle: Impact of controller parameters on stability of MMC-based HVDC systems for offshore wind farms
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The resonance or instability phenomena can happen due to the impedance interactions between the modular multilevel converter (MMC) and the wind power inverter in an MMC-HVDC system connected with offshore wind farms which consist of full-power converters. To analyse the stability of the interconnected system, the impedance-based Nyquist stability analysis method is employed. The analytical ac-side small-signal impedance model of a three-phase MMC is first developed in this paper. The analytical impedance model is verified by means of injecting a small perturbation voltage/current signal in a nonlinear time-domain simulation model. The impacts of the controller parameters on the stability of the interconnected system are then examined by using frequency-domain analysis approach, which can offer guidance for controller parameters design. Finally, the time-domain simulation results validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Study on the fault current transient features of the PV inverter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Lots of studies has presented the steady-state fault features of the photovoltaic (PV) power generator and indicated that the PV power generator can be equivalently replaced by its steady-state fault current model for the fault analysis. However, the disturbance caused by the grid fault is so large that the output of the PV inverter would be saturated, which means the controller of the PV inverter would operate in nonlinear area. Consequently, the fault current transient features of the PV power generator are very complicated and much different from the steady-state fault characteristics. Aimed at it, the fault current transient features of the PV power generator are studied comprehensively in this paper, by taking the non-linearity of the PV inverter controller into consideration. The research results of this paper are of great importance for the establishment of equivalent model of PV power generator and fault analysis of the power grid with PV power generators.

articleTitle: MTDC systems for frequency support base on DC voltage manipulation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper presents control strategies for multi-terminal HVDC systems to provide primary frequency support to connected AC networks via coordinated DC voltage manipulation. Inertia response from DC connected large offshore wind farms can also be incorporated without telecommunication based on the detection of DC voltage derivation. Simulation studies based on a 3-terminal HVDC system connecting one large wind farm and two separate AC networks validate the operation of the system during frequency events.

articleTitle: Modeling and MPPT control of DFIG wind energy system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and maximum power tracking strategies for of variable speed constant frequency (VSCF) doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) system. Firstly, the system simulation model w as construct ed in PSCAD. The grid-side double closed lo op vector control strategy is used to maintain a constant DC bus voltage and to compensate for reactive power at grid, while the stator -flux-oriented vector control is ad opted in rotor-side converter to achieve maxim um power point tracking (MPPT) for the D FIG wind turbine. Secondly, two M PPT method s are discussed and compared for various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Investigation on open-winding PMSG system fed by three level NPC converter and diode converter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In medium and high voltage application, NPC topology has been widely investigated concerning the modulation strategies and control methods. Meanwhile, the open winding configuration is gaining the increasing attention in large power drive field. The semi-controlled open winding PMSG system with the integration of three-level full controlled voltage source converter (VSC) and uncontrolled diode converter will be investigated in this paper. The proposed semi-controlled open winding PMSG system has less switch losses, simpler system configuration and still inherits the advantage of traditional open-winding configuration such as the multilevel modulation effect. Based on the mathematical model of the semi-controlled open winding PMSG system, the control scheme is proposed, which is based on the vector control with rotor flux orientation. Finally, a simulation is built to validate the theoretical investigation on the open winding PMSG system.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of wake interference effects on the downstream wind turbine
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In wind farms, the performance of downstream wind turbines is significantly affected by the upstream turbine wakes. In this study, we focus on the wake interactions of two horizontal-axis wind turbines, and the separation distance has been investigated using a Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) framework. Three models for two in-line turbines arranged with different separation distances have been established using Full Rotor Modelling (FPM) approach. And the flow field in the wake region were analysed to help explain the wake interference effects. The simulation results show that the wake effects depend on the relative positions of wind turbines to a great extent. The wake lateral width increases by almost 31% (at 1D downstream the second wind turbine) caused by the wake interference effects of the first turbine. Additionally, wake effects of upstream wind turbines are not always negative, and they are beneficial for the wake recovery of the downstream turbines under certain circumstances.

articleTitle: Energy management of wind turbine-based DC microgrid utilizing modified differential evolution algorithm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: An energy management optimization model of a wind turbine-based DC microgrid with batteries as the energy storage system is proposed. With introduction of the state of health of battery in this model, the aging process of the storage system is measured. In addition, an improved differential evolution algorithm is proposed which uses the group fitness variance as parameter adjustment indicator and is applied to solve the optimization problem of the DC microgrid system model. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed energy management method, simulations are conducted with results showing that the proposed energy management model can reduce the operation cost caused by the aging of batteries and correct in advance the foreseeable power fluctuations, thus meets the requirement of stably and economically operation of the DC microgrid.

articleTitle: Sensorless operation technique of doubly-fed induction generator connected to DC grid through two full controlled converters
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In order to avoid the drawbacks of the position encoder in DFIG operation, this paper presents a sensorless operation technique when DFIG is connected to DC grid through two full controlled converters. The rotor position phase locked loop (PLL) is employed to estimate the rotor position and speed of DFIG based on the rotor current. The rotor position PLL is parameter insensitive, requiring only an estimation of the magnetization inductance for it to operate and the parameter sensitivity is also analysed. Simulations are conducted to validate the technique presented above.

articleTitle: Design and evaluation of a solar based single inductor multiple outputs LED lighting
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: When driving the paralleled LED strings, the large forward tolerance across the LED will result in the current nonuniformly distributed between each string, which causes LEDs to be overdriven and influence the lifespan. This paper presents a single inductor multiple outputs parallel string LED driver with time multiplexing control schemes. Two kinds of pulse-width modulation schemes are presented and compared. The system architecture, operation principle, simulation and hardware implementation results are demonstrated. The efficiency of the LED driver based on PWM scheme II approaches 88.9% with less than 5% current mismatch between each parallel LED strings, an improvement over PWM scheme I.

articleTitle: Power cost allocation between loads based on demand characteristics and the cooperative game theory
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: With the development of demand response, the potential of various loads to adjust their action of power consumption has been exploited, resulting in loads with different demand characteristics. In allusion to the problem of power cost allocation among loads with different demand characteristics, inflexible load and transferable load, which are the most typical load demand styles, are selected to analyze the irrationality of fixed time-of-use price ( TOUP) and system marginal price (SMP). To deal with the problem, a power cost allocation method based on the theory of cooperation game and Shapley value is proposed in this paper. Examples are discussed and the results reveal that the theory of the cooperative game has wide prospects in dealing with the problem of the power cost allocation when the demand characteristics of the loads are different.

articleTitle: Optimization of the effective reactive power adjustable capacity of DFIG wind farms considering the small signal stability restraints
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In allusion to the coupling relationship between power grid and wind farms, the reactive power regulation characteristics of doubly fed inductive generators (DFIGs) are studied. First of all, taking the wind power integration as a clue, the model of DFIG wind farms for small signal stability analysis is established based on Thevenin equivalence and wind farm equivalence, then an explicit expression for static stability region under specific active-power mode is derivated considering grid-side operation state. On the basis of this expression and taking other steady-state operation constraints into consideration, the mathematical model for reactive power capacity of DFIG wind farms is proposed and interior point method is used to solve the problem. Examples show that the restraints of the small-signal stability must be taken into consideration when determining the adjustable reactive power capability of the DFIG wind farms, and the voltage support ability of the power grid should be also considered because it has direct impact on the static stability and the reactive power regulation ability of wind farms.

Author Keywords: effective adjustable capacity of reactive power

articleTitle: A study of fault statistical analysis and maintenance policy of wind turbine system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: As a clean new energy, wind power draws the attention of the world and wind power generation gets a scale development in recent years. There exposed many problems along with the rapid development of wind power at the same time. The time of most large modern grid connected wind turbine put in to use is not long. Lack of both the accumulation of the practical experience and the research on the fault mode and the operation state bring a lot of problems to the research. This paper mainly makes a statistical analysis on the actual operation failure data of large wind turbines belonging to Huadian new energy company and also analysis the fault conditions of other wind farms. A comparative analysis of the large wind turbines' failure data may provide technical support for the maintenance task in the later, realize the normal and unified maintenance management of the wind power equipment, and improve the level of operation and maintenance which will finally lead to the reduction of the failure rate and maintenance cost.

articleTitle: A novel load-nodal voltage stability index of power system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Voltage stability problems are becoming increasingly evident since large amounts of power are being transferred from long distance and bulk power systems operate close to their stability limits. Accurate recognition of voltage collapse points and rapid analysis of load node voltage stability make it possible for procedures to prevent voltage collapse incidents. These efficacious operations depend on explicit models, rapid indices and very low time cost. In this paper, an efficient method is proposed for finding out voltage collapse point and manifesting voltage stability margins. Although several homologous methods have been used for voltage stability analysis, this developed method is simple, accurate and fast. It is based on a precise model of power network and a terse index of voltage stability margin. The equivalent network model concerns not only the target node but also its connecting buses, which makes it factual and accurate. The index considers both active power and reactive power flows and reflects the voltage stability margins, providing an indication of distance between the operating point and the collapse one. The validity and applicability of the proposed method has been verified through simulation on EPRI-36 bus system.

articleTitle: Fault mode, effects and criticality analysis for overheating fault of wind turbines gearbox and generator
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Aiming at the overheating fault frequently occurred on the wind farm, based on the actual operation data of Guanyun wind farm, the failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) and criticality analysis(CA) of the key equipment (gearbox, generator and converter) has been conducted. Obtained the FMECA analysis table and criticality matrix analysis figure of the wind turbine gearbox, generator and converter under overheating fault, and confirmed the most serious factors of overheating fault. According to the result of overheating fault FMECA analysis, a scheme to solve wind turbines overheating fault and improve the efficiency was proposed combining the actual operation experience of wind turbines and fault statistics. Through the implementation of the scheme, the problems of overheating was solved, and overall improve the performance of wind turbines was improved.

articleTitle: Short-term load forecasting based on the grid method and the time series fuzzy load forecasting method
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Short-term load forecasting refers to daily and weekly load forecasting, which plays a vital role in ensuring security and high quality of power system's economic operation for power generation planning. In short-term load forecasting, load periodicity with the fixed regularity is generally analyzed and random factors like weather are taken into consideration to improve the accuracy of the forecast, however, when large fluctuations of load occur due to failure of high energy-consuming load, there would be a certain forecasting deviation and accuracy would get decreased. To make up for the above deficiencies, firstly the total load is classified into high energy consumption load, general energy consumption load, low energy consumption load and other load according to corresponding power load proportion in the total load, then fuzzy time series method is applied to select similar days of all categories of load, finally grid method and neutral network method are implemented to take different random factors into account to forecast all types of load. Based on those, short-term load can be acquired through superposition of forecast results of all types of load within a same time period. Finally, historical load data of a certain region are applied to load forecasting to verify the feasibility of the classification, and forecasting results demonstrate that the method can improve accuracy effectively.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of large wind farms connected to weak AC networks incorporating PLL dynamics
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Voltage source converter interfaced wind turbines connected to weak grids can induce system instability. A state space model is used in this paper to study the stability of large wind farms. Dynamics of the phase locked loop is integrated to the state space model. The advantage of this model is that it allows study the stability of systems with parallel wind turbines. Studies on the dynamic responses of the system show the importance of including phase locked loop as its existence can induce system instability especially under weak network conditions. This model can be used to study the stability of converter interfaced wind farms and helps to design the converter controller to ensure wind farm system stability when connected to weak grids.

articleTitle: Control strategy for suppressing power oscillation of virtual synchronous generator under unbalanced grid voltage
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) is grid-friendly for integrating distributed generations. However, traditional VSG control will lead to power oscillation under unbalanced grid voltage. To solve this problem, a VSG power oscillation suppressing control strategy is proposed. Firstly, the principle of VSG power fluctuation produced by the unbalanced grid voltage and its distinction from traditional inverter control are demonstrated. Then, a current reference calculation is achieved based on the features of VSG circuit in dq coordinate, which can reduce negative-sequence current under different types of unbalanced voltage. The calculation logic of the method is feasible and power fluctuation can be damped. Finally, the validity and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified through the Matlab/Simulink simulation results.

articleTitle: Direct current control strategy for seamless transfer of voltage source inverter in distributed generation systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper presents a direct current control strategy that enables both islanding operation mode and grid-tied operation mode of three-phase inverter in distributed generation systems. With no need for switching between two corresponding modes or critical islanding detection, the proposed control strategy composes two current control loops, including an inductor current loop and a direct capacitor current loop are cascaded in the synchronous reference frame. In the grid-tied mode, the three-phase inverter is regulated as a current source just by the inductor current loop. The capacitor current limiter can be used to regulate the load voltage and guarantee the voltage quality upon the occurrence of islanding. Additionally, this paper presents the parameters design of the control strategy. Finally, the proposed control strategy is verified by the simulation result.

articleTitle: Mechanical DC circuit breakers and FBSM-based MMCs in a high-voltage MTDC network: Coordinated operation for network riding through DC fault
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: DC circuit breaker is of vital importance for security in a high voltage (HV) multi-terminal DC (MTDC) network, particularly in the HV MTDC based on voltage source converters (VSCs) that are typically based on two-level, neutral point clamed (NPC) three-level and modular multilevel. Mechanical DC circuit breaker characterized with low costs and losses has been widely used in the conventional LCC-based HV MTDC network, but cannot be directly applied in the VSC-based HV MTDC due to its slow response and limited breaking capacity. On the other hand, the technology of hybrid DC circuit breaker is immature at present, which has been demonstrated with prototype and cannot be employed in HV (≥320kV) applications in over ten years. As a result, DC circuit breaker has become an obstacle for HV MTDC development. This paper presents a kind of coordinated operation between mechanical DC breakers and full-bridge sub-module (FBSM) based MMCs to guarantee DC fault ride-through in a HV MTDC network. The proposed coordination strategy is dependent on the DC fault current controllability provided by FBSM-based MMC. Specifically, the capability of FBSM's negative level is adopted to change the common-mode component of MMC arm's reference voltage, which can restrain the fault current to the maximum operation threshold of mechanical DC circuit breaker. This scheme can reduce the demand of breaking capacity and response time for mechanical DC circuit breaker, which thus shows great potential in the applications of HV MMC-based MTDC network. The effectiveness and validity of the coordinated operation is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Autonomous hybrid renewable energy system optimization for minimum cost
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The concept of microgrids based on locally available renewable energy sources (RES) is becoming very popular in remote locations. They are going to play a significant role in future power systems providing economical, reliable and environmental benefits as compare to the existing power systems. But it can be only achieved by providing considerable attention and efforts to resolve the copious economic, commercial, and technical challenges incurred in their development. This work presents an economic evaluation considering the installation and operating cost of such a microgrid for remote terrains. An optimization problem is formulated for capital cost and running costs. A comparative cost analysis of different configurations of hybrid renewable energy resource system (HRES) is carried out using practical data. It is found that hybrid energy system consisting of solar/wind/diesel generator along with battery is the most feasible system. With the appearance of such microgrids the current way of expanding the electricity demand will revolutionize, exclusively for remote location being served below par by the customary power system.

articleTitle: Effects of swing equation-based inertial response (SEBIR) control on penetration limits of non-synchronous generation in the GB power system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper investigates the limits to penetration levels of non-synchronous generation (NSG) in a power system and how this may be increased. Reduced system inertia, arising from high penetrations of NSG, is one of the main issues that may increase the risk of system instability in various guises. Swing equation-based inertial response (SEBIR) control, often referred to using a variety of terms, is considered to be a potential solution that can enable converter-interfaced generation to support the system during and after disturbances. However, the effects of SEBIR on system operability and its ability to increase the NSG penetration limits and improve system strength under high NSG scenarios has not been fully investigated. The paper presents the implementation of SEBIR control within a simplified model of the future Great Britain (GB) transmission model, created using DIgSILENT PowerFactory. Using the model, the instantaneous penetration level limits of NSG in terms of both transient and steady-state stability are investigated with and without SEBIR control applied to the NSG. The capability of SEBIR in enabling additional active power output from NSG and improving system frequency response under a loss of infeed event is investigated and it is shown how SEBIR can assist in increasing NSG penetration levels, but that further work is required to understand certain phenomena that have been observed.

articleTitle: Virtual inertia control of grid-connected wind farms
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: With the penetration level of wind power into the gird continuously increasing, the impact of wind farms on dynamic stability of power systems is significantly highlighted. It is necessary for grid-connected wind farms to provide ancillary services, such as active power control, frequency regulation and damping control. Currently, most of the published papers have already studied the virtual inertia control and its effects on improving the stability of system frequency and small-signal stability. A frequency control loop is added to the active power control system of wind farms, which can be utilized to make wind farms have the ability of fast response to system frequency deviation following the appearance of the power imbalance, thus increasing the stability of system frequency. This paper summarizes the influencing characteristics of different virtual inertia control strategies, various control parameters and their effects on system small-signal stability and torsional oscillations. Furthermore, the control architecture, designing of the controller and integrated methodology with damping control are deeply studied. The research hotspots of virtual inertia control and its development trends are introduced. This paper also presents some issues to be researched in the near future.

articleTitle: Optimization of a solar based water pumping system using a high step up inverter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Solar power is an attractive source of energy, free, abundant and not polluting the atmosphere. However, due to the low efficiency of current photovoltaic cells, conversion of sunlight into electrical power is very poor, and it is irradiance level, array temperature dependents, this efficiency further decreases if there is no impedance matching between photovoltaic panels output and the load to ensure that the maximum power transfer theorem is fulfilled. This paper describes operation of a water pumping system consisting of a Centrifugal pump coupled to a BLDC motor, accompanying a single stage high step up inverter fed by photovoltaic arrays. The designed inverter has got the capability of performing DC boost/buck, DC-AC inversion and fast Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT). Particular Swarm optimization Fuzzy logic based MPPT algorithm is used to track the Maximum Power Point (MPP) of the solar panel by providing dedicated gating signals to power switches. The designed water pumping system has been implemented and modelled in Matlab/Simulink; simulated results show the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method in increasing pumping performances.

articleTitle: Power loss analysis and optimization of three-level T-type converter based on hybrid devices
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper details the loss model of T-type converter using an improved method which is quite simple. The method utilizes the current and voltage information from simulation model in which the impact of the PWM methods, dead time and devices on the power losses are involved. Thus, the influences of different PWM methods and devices are analysed. Based on the results, a low-voltage three phase 10kW T-type inverter equipped with hybrid devices is implemented. Results show that the discontinuous SVPWM (DPWM1) achieves higher efficiency than continuous SVPWM. Based on the loss distribution of the devices in the bridge, the hybrid device combination of CoolMOS/FWD as main switch and IGBT/SiC diode as auxiliary switches are utilized in the prototype. It can exploit the potential of these devices. The maximum efficiency of the prototype reaches at 99.2% at 20 kHz switching frequency.

articleTitle: Unit commitment considering coordinated dispatch of large scale electric vehicles and wind power generation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Assuming that all electric vehicles (EVs) integrated to the grid are managed by aggregators, it is possible to make full use of the controllability of the charging EVs. Based on this, the charging load of each EV aggregator is defined as one of the optimal scheduling variables in the unit commitment (UC) model. This can be accomplished by assessing the upper and lower limit of charging load of each EV aggregator in different scenarios, which is simulated by Monte Carlo method. According to this, a UC model is proposed for optimal coordination of EV aggregators and wind generation, considering the EV owner's requirement, the range of charging load and the unit constraints. Using the10-units system as the test system, the results of UC models with different EVs charging strategies and the wind power integration indicators such as utilization rate are investigated. Simulation results show that both the abandoned wind power and the unit operating costs can be decreased more effectively in the proposed UC model.

articleTitle: A generation-reserve co-optimization dispatching model for wind power integrated power system based on risk reserve constraints
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The stochastic fluctuation of wind farm outputs and the difficulties to accurately predict, adjust and control bring problems in generation dispatch and reserve decision of power system with large scale wind power integration. Based on the probabilistic characteristics of wind power and load forecast errors, a new random variable is introduced and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) is adopted to calculate the risk reserve capacity. Considering uncertain factors such as equipment failure, prediction errors of loads and wind power, a novel risk reserve constrained generation and operating reserve optimal dispatching model is proposed. Simulation results on a modified IEEE 39-bus system show that the proposed method is able to strike the balance between reliability and economy of the wind power system by setting the value of confidence level and give optimal scheme for the allocation of thermal power outputs and reserve among the generation units.

articleTitle: Circulating-current analysis and power sharing control of parallel inverters with different capacities
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper proposes control methods to achieve accurate active and reactive power sharing of parallel multi-inverters in proportion to their capacities. Firstly, according to physical properties of parallel inverters' output power, the interaction mechanism between circulating-current and load-sharing is elaborated. Conditions for a control strategy to result in specified power sharing and minimum circulating-current are discussed based on the assumption that transmission lines are inductive. Limited effectiveness of traditional droop control is deeply analysed. An improved droop control strategy is proposed to achieve accurate proportional power sharing results unaffected by the impedance of lines. Moreover, since lines in microgrid are not inductive in practice, coupling of active and reactive power is observed on lines. Based on improved droop control, a new control strategy with added virtual reactance is furtherly proposed to enable decoupling control of active and reactive power sharing. The effectiveness of theoretical analyses and proposed control strategies in this paper is verified by PSCAD/EMTDC simulation results.

articleTitle: Invsetigation of PV inverter MPPT efficiency test platform
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In this paper, the test platform of PV inverter MPPT efficiency is researched. The test method of PV inverter MPPT efficiency is analyzed according to evaluation index of PV inverter MPPT efficiency. Based on the MPPT efficiency test method, The PV array simulation should output P-V curve of PV array in different irradiance and different type of PV module. A 500kW PV inverter MPPT efficiency is tested and evaluated by this platform. The test results verify the validity of the test platform which analyzed in this paper.

articleTitle: Damping DFIG-associated SSR with subsynchronous suppression filters: A case study on a practical wind farm system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The interaction between the converter controllers of doubly-fed induction generators (DFIGs) and fixed series compensation tends to cause a new type of subsynchronous resonance (SSR), or subsynchronous control interaction. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel scheme to deactivate such an interaction by embedding subsynchronous suppression filters (SSFs) into DFIG's converter controllers. Its ability to stabilize SSR is validated by applying it to a practical wind farm system in North China, which has experienced many SSR events. The electromagnetic model incorporating multiple DFIG-based wind farms and series-compensated transmissions is established. Then its SSR characteristics are investigated and used to design SSF's parameters. Two SSF schemes are developed for the target system. The high-cost scheme has all DFIGs equipped with SSFs while a more cost-effective scheme is also designed, which only needs to add SSFs to an optimized number of DFIGs. Simulation results have verified the effectiveness of both schemes in guaranteeing the stability of SSR under all possible operating conditions. In practice, the latter scheme is preferred because of its low cost and sufficient performance.

articleTitle: Geothermal energy, a key point in energy and development in China
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Energy consumption, environmental protection and pollution would be huge challenges for China in near future especially while at the moment economic growth is pushing the energy infrastructure and consumption in a higher amount. This paper presents the renewable energy technologies as an approach to save and guarantee China's economy and energy demand against future challenges. Focusing on the potential of geothermal energy in China, the Shaanxi province can be benefited from enormous advantages of this clean energy. Both shallow and deep geothermal energy are studied and the results show the performance of the proposed method for Shaanxi province and Xian city.

articleTitle: Power coupling analysis of inverters based on relative gain method and decoupling control based on feedforward compensation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The output active and reactive power of inverter-interfaced distributed generator are coupling when the line is both resistive and inductive. In this paper, it first indicates the reasons and necessity of decoupling the output active and reactive power. Then according to the line transmission power expression it analyzes the power coupling based on the relative gain method and also presents the calculation method and meaning of the coupling degree. Then, a decoupling algorithm based on the feed-forward compensation is proposed. At last, a simulation example is designed and the three groups of PSCAD/EMTDC simulation diagrams show that the proposed feedforward compensation decoupling method has good decoupling performance.

articleTitle: Research on economic operation of grid-connected DC microgrid
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The application of DC microgrid is conductive to the integration of renewable energy sources into the distribution system and the improvement of power system flexibility. The economic operation of DC microgrid is a significant aspect of DC microgrid development. In this paper, an optimal scheduling model considering the characteristics of DC microgrid, which contains economic cost, environmental cost, net loss and various constraints, has been established. Then the improved hybrid particle swarm optimization (HPSO) algorithm was used to solve the model. Finally, the simulation results were analyzed, which verified the validity and effectivity of the proposed optimization strategy.

articleTitle: An optimal strategy for load recovery considering renewable energy resource integration
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Consider the huge economic losses from large power blackouts, how to quickly and effectively restore loads becomes particularly significant. In this paper, a formulation for the load restoration is proposed and discussed to find the load recovery sequence and restore system quickly with consideration of the impacts of renewable energy resources (RERs) integration on the process of load restoration. The proposed load restoration model involves load importance and the distance between load and RERs. And a coefficient is introduced to adjust the level of balance between the importance and the distance according to different requirements. In addition, the frequency factor is considered during optimization. Finally, the greedy algorithm is employed to solve the proposed model based on the IEEE standard test system as benchmark, and the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and validity of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: The cumulative effect analysis of the short-circuit current of the key equipment in power systems based on the batch operations of PSD-BPA software
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Safe and reliable operation of the power grid equipment directly relates to the safety and reliability of power systems in the electric power systems. When the short circuit fault occurs in the power grid, over-current flows through the electric devices will produce certain effects on the equipment. Long-term cumulative effect of many times faults cause significant influence on the key equipment. Currently, there is lack of an effective quantitative analysis method in the cumulative effect of the short circuit current which aimed at key equipment (transformer, circuit breaker, etc.) in the power systems. This paper presents a fault short-circuit current cumulative effect analysis model, based on the PSD-BPA software and results of the batching calculation of the short-circuit current program, according to the fault occurrence time, the actual fault type and system operation parameters. The paper presents the results of the cumulative effect of a fault in the Jiangsu power grid. Finally, it puts forward the ideas of the graphical display of application in the power systems. The proposed method can be used to sort the equipment according to the history fault current cumulative effect of the equipment, and provide early warning and maintenance of the equipment, which will help to improve the safe and stable operation of the power grid.

articleTitle: Cost benefit analysis of combined storage and distribution generation systems in smart distribution grid
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: A novel cost benefit analysis approach is proposed for the storage and distribution power and their combination when they are applied in smart distribution grid. The approach includes two parts, the cost-benefit analysis part and the operation simulation part. A life cycle cost analysis is addressed for the cost benefit analysis, which takes the working life of storages and distribution generations (PV in this case) into account. The operation simulation part takes charge in the simulation of the system, offers key parameters for the cost benefit analysis in real time based on the cost and the boundary conditions of the system. In such way, the bottom to up approach gives better understanding of the relation between cost and benefit. In particular, the comprehensive benefit of battery energy storage system (BESS) together with photovoltaic systems when applied in a given distribution grid is analysed, suggestions for the arrangement of the system are listed according to the simulation results.

articleTitle: External parameters contribution in domestic load forecasting using neural network
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Domestic demand prediction is very important for home energy management system and also for peak reduction in the power system network. In this work, for precise prediction of power demand, external parameters, such as temperature and solar radiation, are considered and included in the prediction model for improving prediction performance. Power prediction models for coming hours' power demand estimation are built using neural network based on hourly power consumptions data with / without ambient temperature data and global solar irradiation (GSI) data respectively. In this work, a typical Southern Norwegian household demand has been considered. As a result, both ambient temperature and GSI data are effective on improving the prediction performance on certain level, and the prediction performs better when ambient temperature and GSI are included together.

articleTitle: Site and size selection strategies of energy storage system based on power supply and storage capability index
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Energy Storage System (ESS) is the implementation basis of active control in smart distribution grid, benefiting the smoothing of output power, load fluctuations, and the voltage quality. Firstly, a Supply and Storage Capacity Index (SSC) considering the variety constraints of power conversion, power flow and network topology is proposed, so as to quantitatively analyse the charging and discharging capability of ESS interconnected into power grid. Secondly, the safe operation objective function of the load transfer capability, which is based on SSC, is calculated. This can be used to evaluate the safety margin of ESS and DG integrated distribution network. Based on these, the ESS sitting and sizing problem, which considers both the system security and economics, is solved with the improved nondominated sorting genetic algorithm. The proposed method has been validated in a representative area in China, which is the pilot demonstration region in Guizhou province according to the project of research and application of intermittent energy consumption and optimization for Active Distribution Network, which is supported by the National High-tech R&D Program (863) of China.

articleTitle: Study on the influence factors of commutation failure in MIDC systems
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Based on the commutation failure generation theory, This paper analyzes the influence factors of multi-infeed dc (MIDC) transmission systems, then introduces the concept of multi-infeed short circuit, demonstrates the influence of MISCR on extinction angle and the change regulation in detail.Meanwhile through mathematical derivation, the changing relations of other parameters and extinction angle can be qualitatively explained, which can directly reflect the influence of various parameters on commutation failure. Finally, according to the results of the research, the conclusion meeting the actual situation is drawn.

articleTitle: Probabilistic unit commitment in multi-area grids with high renewable energy penetration by using dynamic programming based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Nowadays, economic and environmental requirements are increased. Therefore, this paper presents a proposed solution of the unit commitment problem for a multi-area grid, which contains conventional and renewable energy sources and storage units. To ensure optimum and economic operation with the stochastic nature sources, it is essential to develop an efficient forecasting model for renewable power generation. Forecasting model was built by using a hybrid Markov to forecast solar power, while, auto regressive integrated moving average model is used to predict wind power. Unit commitment problem incorporate with forecasting model to develop probabilistic unit commitment. The proposed formulation is subject to multi-constraints. To overcome the variation and error of renewable power forecasting, the reserve coefficient is modified to develop two new reserves; up reserve and down reserve. The optimization algorithm used to solve probabilistic unit commitment is Dynamic programming based on Neural Network. The system under study in this paper is a standard IEEE 30, with wind speed and solar radiation data are based on the available data of the city of Florida in USA.

articleTitle: Risk assessment of distribution network considering randomness of photovoltaic generation
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Photovoltaic power is widely favoured because of its safety, short construction period and other advantages. However, the randomness of photovoltaic power makes it different from traditional generation so that it's necessary to be considered in the safety analysis of power grid. In this paper, considering the randomness of photovoltaic power, line overload risk index and node low voltage risk index are established by combining the risk theory with K (N - 1 + 1) principle for distribution network which is developed from traditional (N-1) deterministic principle. IEEE three-feeder example system is applied to investigate the influence of photovoltaic power system on the risk of distribution network. And test results show that photovoltaic power generation system connected to distribution network can effectively reduce the risk of distribution network.

articleTitle: Transient power angle stability analysis of emergency wind turbine tripping
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: With the development of wind power generation, the wind turbine tripping has become an effective emergency control measure. Its mechanism has become a research focus. On basis of the EEAC theory and the influence of wind turbine tripping on system transient stability, this article indicates the mechanism for the rotor-angle stability of synchronous generators. At the time of emergency control, wind turbine tripping leads to change of synchronous generators, such as the mutation of electromagnetic power and the variation of retardation area. As a consequence of these change, the transient power angle stability is suffered. In this context, the analytic expression of electromagnetic power mutation is derived. The factors that influence the rotor acceleration mutation amount are also obtained. The viability of the method is demonstrated through the simulation.

articleTitle: Aggregated dynamic model of grid-connected PV generation farms
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper establishes the aggregated transfer function model of a large-scale PV power generation farm connected to a multi-machine power system for the study of power system small-signal angular stability. The aggregated model can reduce the computational burden and complexity brought about by the inclusion of dynamics of the grid-connected largescale PV farm significantly. In the case that the parameters of the PV farm are not available, it is proposed in the paper that a frequency-response aggregated model of the PV farm can be obtained via a field test. Then the frequency-response model can be used to derive the aggregated transfer function model. In the paper, an example power system connected with largescale PV farms is presented to demonstrate and validate the application of the aggregated model proposed.

articleTitle: Substation inspection based on wearable devices and big data technology
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Substation inspection is one of the most important works of keeping the safe and stable operation of the substation in the power systems. The study is based on the latest wearable and large data services technology, adopting human judgment and analysis capabilities as the center of new intelligent substation inspection technology. It actually has many innovations though the integrated research and application of virtualization, big data, smart wearable devices and other technologies. For example, taking advantage of Google glasses to develop visualization professional applications, making use of intelligent wearable technology innovation to distinguish life feature, adopting the big data of the power network to do services of big data applications on substation inspection.

articleTitle: A control strategy in a stationary frame for grid-connected inverter with LCL filter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: By analyzing the mathematical model of the three-phase grid-connected inverter with LCL filter in the two-phase stationary coordinates, a quasi-PR controller which can track the grid current without steady error in stationary coordinates is proposed in this paper. To restrain the resonance caused by the insufficient damping, the capacitor current feedback is introduced to realize active damping. According to the requests of the stability, stability margin and steady-state error, the capacitor current feedback coefficient, resonant gain and proportional factor could be designed, respectively, by using frequency theory. The effectiveness of the adopted parameters design method and feasibility of the proposed control strategy are verified by simulation and experiment results.

articleTitle: Maximum power point tracking of wind turbine based on optimal power curve detection under variable wind speed
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper aims to propose a new control algorithm to automatically detect the optimal power-speed curve of a wind energy conversion system, under variable wind speed, for maximum power point tracking (MPPT). The optimal power speed curve is determined by controlling the wind turbine with a staircase rotor speed set-points to obtain the maximum power points accurately with an optimizing algorithm. The control algorithm is implemented experimentally on a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG), which is directly coupled to a wind turbine emulated by a DC motor. The experimental results validate that the power curve is determined and optimized accurately with the proposed algorithm. Therefore, the wind turbine can be controlled to track the maximum power coefficient without needing prior knowledge of the wind turbine characteristics.

articleTitle: Location of single phase disconnection fault with non-grounding in distribution grid based on positive sequence voltage
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: A fault location method of single phase disconnection fault with non-grounding is proposed which is based on the characteristic of positive sequence voltage decrease after fault occurs. Based on three-phase voltage of distribution transformers, positive sequence voltage is calculated using the method of symmetrical components. The positive sequence voltage at the high voltage side (HV side) of a distribution transformer located behind the fault point is far less than that at the front of it or at a non-fault distribution line, and the positive sequence voltage at the low voltage side (LV side) behind the fault point becomes about 50% of that before the fault occurs. According to characteristic of positive sequence voltage decreasing, the paper calculates the positive sequence voltage of each load point in real time. If the positive sequence voltage of a load point at a time becomes significantly smaller with the positive sequence voltage of its' downstream load point at the same time becoming smaller too and the positive sequence voltage of its' upstream load point without changing, the fault is single phase disconnection fault with non-grounding. Its' location is between the load point and its' upstream load point. Simulation studies fully verify the validity of the algorithm.

Author Keywords: single phase disconnection fault with non-grounding

articleTitle: Study on the stability mechanism of power system with large scale wind power integration
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In power system electro-mechanical transients, wind power with power electronic interface is more capable of controlling active power compared to synchronous generator, but less capable of controlling voltage. Wind power is beneficial to transient rotor angle stability because it improves the deceleration of synchronous generator, but it is detrimental to transient voltage stability. A mechanism of wind power inducing voltage instability is studied. When the proportion of wind power in the system increases, the dominant stability problem changes from rotor angle stability to voltage stability, and the stability of the system first gets better then gets worse.

articleTitle: Research on VSC-MTDC for grid integration of wind farm
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Developing the Voltage Source Converter (VSC) based multi-terminal HVDC (MTDC) grid or a DC grid has re-emerged in recent years due to the increasing penetration of renewable energy generation and the need for alternative power routes. This paper studies connection topologies of offshore wind farm Grid integration via VSC-MTDC with a focus on their dynamic responses to disturbance, e.g. Grid fault, wind farm failure. The simulation results in PSCAD show parallel connection is more robust than series connection in terms of transient stability when a VSC-MTDC system recovers from faults in AC system and shut-down of a wind farm offshore converter. An optimisation of PI control parameters in VSC-MTDC is also performed using the Simplex method. It is found that the optimisation brings improvement to dynamic stability of the system.

articleTitle: Protection challenges in future converter dominated power systems: Demonstration through simulation and hardware tests
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: A model of a converter source capable of providing a controllable fault response is introduced to analyse the performance of protection in future power system scenarios. Using a reduced power system model of the National Grid transmission system in Great Britain, a comprehensive set of tests of protection performance are performed to verify how protection systems may be impacted by the introduction of converter-interfaced energy sources and infeeds. Converters with a range of different types of fault response are modelled, as grid codes defining converter response to AC system fault are not completely specific at the present time. The simulated data are injected into an actual protection relay through secondary injection equipment and also to a dynamic protection relay model through simulation, and the results are analysed and compared. The initial results show that there can be a degree of negative influence on protection system performance in converter-dominated scenarios where the power system is relatively "weak", primarily in the form of longer operating times in certain scenarios. The paper concludes with analysis of results and an overview of on-going and future work to broaden the investigations.

articleTitle: Comparison of several MPPT methods for PV arrays under partially shaded conditions
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In this paper, the best load line based two-stage MPPT, the analog locating circuit, the real maximum power point tracking (RMPPT) proposed by Ji Young-Hyok, Fibonacci search based MPPT and their variations are compared by simulation at Matlab/Simulink platform under several partially shaded conditions with a DC/DC circuit. These MPPT techniques are compared at global maxima tracking, steady-state oscillation, dynamic performance, the cumulative power generating, convergence speed, implementation complexity etc. In addition, a further discussion of two-stage MPPT and RMPPT are made.

articleTitle: Review on protection issues of low-voltage distribution network with multiple power-electronic-converter-interfaced distribution energy resources
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The realisation of an eventual low-voltage (LV) Smart Grid with a complete communication infrastructure is a gradual process. During this evolution the protection scheme of distribution networks should be continuously adapted and optimised to fit the protection and cost requirements at the time. This paper aims to review practices and research around the design of an effective, adaptive and economical distribution network protection scheme. The background of this topic is introduced and potential problems are defined from conventional protection theories and new Smart Grid technologies. Challenges are identified with possible solutions defined as a pathway to the ultimate flexible and reliable LV protection systems.

articleTitle: Individual pitch control strategy of wind turbine to reduce load fluctuations and torque ripples
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Wind velocity distribution differences in wind wheel rotation plane caused by wind shear and tower shadow, not only causes load fluctuations of wind turbine blades, but also leads to pulsations of wind turbine aerodynamic torque and output power. In order to reduce the influence of wind shear and tower shadow on the fluctuations of three-bladed wind turbine, an individual pitch control strategy based on the pitch angle signal adjusted jointly by wind turbine output power and rotor azimuth angle is proposed. A band-pass filter is designed to filter out the three times pulsating component of the wind turbine output power, and a PID controller is used to obtain regulatory signal of pitch angle, which is then converted to tiny variable of each blade combining with the azimuth angle signal and superimposed to the reference pitch angle of the collective pitch control. Simulation results on GH Bladed platform show that the proposed individual pitch control strategy is effective to smooth blade load fluctuation, diminish aerodynamic torque ripple, reduce rotor fatigue damage, and prolong life time of wind turbine.

articleTitle: Application of SOM neural network in fault diagnosis of wind turbine
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Wind power plays an important role in the electric power industry. However, wind turbines are prone to failures because of the extreme environment. The traditional methods for condition monitoring and fault diagnosis require large amounts of time and energy. Meanwhile, we cannot collect all the information about fault, so BP neural network cannot make a correct diagnosis. Therefore, self-organizing map (SOM) neural network is applied to the vibration fault diagnosis of wind turbine. The network is trained using sample data of normal operating condition. According to the position of the detection sample output neurons in the output layer, we can judge whether the wind turbine occurs faults or not. The results have shown that the proposed method can diagnose wind turbine faults effectively.

articleTitle: Virtual inertia control of wind-battery-based islanded DC micro-grid
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The battery-based islanded DC micro-grid possesses low inertia at the moment when the system is disturbed due to the access of a large number of power electric converters. In this paper, to optimize the use of rotational kinetic energy concealed in DC micro-grid, a virtual inertia control strategy for DC micro-grid is proposed through associating DC bus voltage with the speed regulation of PMSG. Take the wind battery-based islanded DC micro-grid for example, this paper analyses the system inertia previously, and then its smallsignal models are derived. The system stability is compared between with and without virtual inertia control and the results demonstrate that the system stability can be enhanced remarkably when the virtual inertia control strategy is added into DC micro-grid. Also the model is established in MATLAB/SIMULINK and the simulation results validate that the virtual inertia control not only can enhance the system transient stability but also can protect the battery and even prolong the service life of it.

articleTitle: A new paradigm for the relationship between power suppliers and users through EE services
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: With the new turn of power industry reform coming, there will be potentially fierce competitions of the power retail market by China's open policy. To keep leading position as usual, traditional power suppliers, like the distribution companies owned by the State Grid and Southern Grid, are seeking solutions to compete the retail market. This paper describes a new paradigm for the state owned traditional power suppliers to help them compete in the retail market, which includes several interactive service programs between the power suppliers and their users. Through the programs, power suppliers draw up agreements with customers to get their active participating commitments and the authorization of collecting and processing of power consumption data. Then power suppliers or the third value added service providers process and mine power usage data to profile a single user or its similar peers' power usage characteristics. Based on the profiles the programs provide the customers with services, such as energy efficiency (EE) monitoring, EE benchmarking, power-saving schemes, even direct control of the user's electrical appliances / equipment under a predefined rules. To help decision makers better understand the paradigm, this paper also introduces some best practices by the world leading utilities and third party service providers.

articleTitle: Research on the improvement of LVRT ability of an actual DFIG-type wind farm with Crowbar and SVG
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: As one reactive power compensation device, the SVG can effectively improve the LVRT (low-voltage ride-through) ability of wind generator and prevent large-scale wind power off-grid. This paper analyses the improvement of LVRT ability of an actual DFIG-type wind farm with Crowbar and SVG. Firstly, the Model and control of SVG and Crowbar are presented, and then, the coordination of SVG and Crowbar is introduced. Finally, the improvement of LVRT with SVG and Crowbar for an actual DFIG-type wind farms is validated through simulation.

articleTitle: Virtual video and real-time data demonstration for smart substation inspection based on Google glasses
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Substation inspection is not only one of the most important means of ensuring safe and stable operation of equipment, but also a significant way of timely detecting the dominant and recessive defect of the equipment, and preventing the accidents. This paper presents the virtual video and real-time data demonstration used for smart substation inspection based on the latest wearable services technology (such as Google glass). Google Glass is hands-free and uses augmented reality and voice activation to project useful data into our field of vision. A key use-case of google glass could be to allow a field crew out in the substation to be able to identify all relevant data for the network at the crew's current location. From this interface, they could navigate through all the data for a transformer, such as voltage, current, temperature etc. and identify its location in the GIS and view a single-line diagram, query into its asset history, maintenance history, manufacturer information and catalogue etc.

articleTitle: Stochastic chance constraint with discrete probabilities of wind sources in economic dispatch
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In this paper, wind power (WP) modelling is improved in Economic Dispatch (ED). These proposed models are more realistic, practical, and accurate models. Hence the proposed models minimize the risk due to uncertainty. The stochastic probability of stochastic WP based on the Weibull probability density function is included in the ED model as a stochastic chance constraint; the here-and-now strategy. This strategy avoids the probabilistic infeasibility of the Wait-and-See strategy. The correlated bivariate distribution including continuous and discrete probabilities has been derived to be used as stochastic chance constraint. As the correlated bivariate Weibull distribution is very complex and difficult mathematically and is limited to two random variables (RVs) only, the correlated Normal distribution has been proposed to model wind sources especially for more than two random variables. The Augmented Lagrangian Genetic Algorithm has been used to obtain the optimal solutions. Ten unit test system has been used to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed models. Based on presented models, it is shown that, the results obtained provide direct guidelines for system operators to make correct decisions to schedule the power systems with wind power. It can be concluded that the proposed models provide valuable information and suggestions for safe, reliable, and economic power systems operation.

articleTitle: A static reactive power coordination control strategy of solar PV plant considering voltage and power factor
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The operation of large-scale grid-connected solar photovoltaic (PV) plants may cause the voltage fluctuation issue, which will affect the stable operation of power system. In order to reduce the adverse effects and power network loss caused by PV plants, the reactive power control of PV plant is investigated and a novel coordination control strategy considering both voltage and power factor is proposed in this paper. First, the effect of active and reactive power on voltage of interconnection point is analysed. Second, an eleven-zone reactive power control strategy is proposed, while nine-zone reactive power control strategy is always used today, the proposed strategy adopts both voltage and power factor of interconnection point as criterion to conduct respective controlling. At last, based on performance verification platform of solar PV plant power control system developed by authors, the feasibility and correctness of proposed elevenzone reactive power control strategy are proved by practices in a real solar PV plant grid integration project.

articleTitle: Design of universal research platform for renewable energy connected to grid with power electronic devices
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: The widely spread application of renewable energy by power electronic devices brings more and more challenges in voltage regulation, power flow control and power quality. Therefore, higher standards are put forward for variety of renewable energy grid-connected power electronic devices. According to these standards and requirements of its own performance, such as power generation efficiency, a universal research platform for renewable energy grid-connected power electronic devices is introduced. Research platform consists of programmable DC source, impedance adjustable lines, intelligent circuit breaker and programmable AC source, and they are all controlled by a central control software. By this research platform, the power grid fault and variety working conditions are simulated. And a multi-point data acquisition system which can synchronize sampling multiple nodes' waveform is built on Labview. Hence research on multiple power electronic devices operating in parallel can be carried out on this research platform. A wind- photovoltaic-battery combined running case is given to illustrate the platform suitable for a variety of test of different types of renewable energy power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Wind turbine fault diagnosis based on unscented Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: A wind turbine is a nonlinear system with multi-variables that can be measured subject to considerable noise. To realize intelligent fault detection for wind turbines as part of condition monitoring, an unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) approach, widely used for signal tracking of nonlinear systems, is adopted in this paper. Its capability for reliable fault detection is assessed. A model has been developed to represent temperature variation of generator stator winding of a healthy wind turbine under operational conditions. This model is developed based on heat generation principle within the stator winding and the thermal dynamics of heat loss. This model is further incorporated into an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) for generator temperature prediction and thus fault detection. Two failure modes are introduced into the thermal model, which results are compared with predicted results of the UKF model. Effectiveness of the UKF for wind turbine fault detection is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research on modelling and verification for PV power plants with AVC system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation has the characteristic property of inherent randomness and volatility, which will cause voltage fluctuation in the point of interconnection (POI). Therefore, the PV power station is required to provide the ability for regulating the voltage of the POI. In order to meet the dispatching requirements, PV power station needs to assemble the automatic voltage control (AVC) system, which can coordinated regulate all kinds of reactive power resource to realize voltage regulating function. The paper researches on the AVC system control strategy. With a PV power station in northwest as an example, this paper establishes the PV power station model installing the AVC system based on the DIgSILENT. Combining with the field measured data and simulation results, the accuracy of the PV power station model is verified.

articleTitle: A model predictive control algorithm applied in T-type three-level power conversion system
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has been widely used in grid-connected battery energy storage system. This paper addresses model power predictive control in T-type three-level power conversion system. A model predictive control algorithm based on T-type three-level converter is proposed. Compared to traditional neutral point clamped (NPC) three-level converter, T-type three-level converter suffers no output phase voltage jump limitation thus more outstanding performance by MPC can be achieved. This paper describes the model of T-type three-level converter as well as the principle of model predictive control algorithm. Moreover, a geometrical analysis method has been used to demonstrate that the performance of T-type converter is superior to NPC converter. The simulation results verify the feasibility of former analysis.

articleTitle: Probabilistic rotor angular stability considering renewable power generations — A survey
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: With the integration of large scale renewable power generations (e.g. Wind power generations) and new types of electric loads (e.g. Electrical vehicles), more and more stochastic factors are being introduced into power systems. Traditionally, power system rotor angle stability issues are treated under deterministic domain which means all the parameters involved are unchanged during the analysis. Although deterministic approaches have been used widely for decades, they might not be able to give a real appraisal on power system rotor angle stability due to the fact that the power system is stochastic in nature. In this paper, a comprehensive review on the topic of probabilistic power system rotor angle stability analysis which includes probabilistic small signal stability analysis (PSSSA) and probabilistic transient stability analysis (PTSA) is presented. The paper first reviews three main methodologies which are currently being used in PSSSA and a comparison among them is made. The development and main approaches of PTSA are given afterwards.

articleTitle: Cloud identification model for sky images based on Otsu
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Irradiance changes caused by clouds movement are the main factors, which lead to mutation of photovoltaic power. In order to increase the accuracy of the ultra-short-term photovoltaic power prediction, based on of clouds images, the cloud identification for sky images is one of the primary aspects for improving photovoltaic power accuracy. A cloud identification model for sky images is established based on Otsu. Firstly, a series of sky images are collected by Total Sky Imager (TSI) with the regions of clouds and sky are distinguished. Secondly, the color features (based on RGB values) of pixels in sample images and the spectral and texture features of the whole image are extracted; Finally, we established a cloud identification model for sky images based on Otsu according to the clouds' and sky areas' division and the general characteristics featured by pixels and images. The simulated results show that the model in this paper can identify the clouds in a sky images effectively.

articleTitle: An integrated control strategy of PMSG-based wind turbine generation system to improve its fault ride-through capability by using an energy storage device
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: In order to improve the fault ride-though (FRT) capability of PMSG-based wind turbine generation system, an energy storage system composed of ultracapacitor (UC) and bidirectional Buck-Boost converter (BDBBC) paralleled to the DC-link of the dual PWM converter is used in this paper. The integrated control strategy for both grid-side converter (GSC) and BDBBC has been presented, which has two working modes. Under normal grid operation, it works in normal mode where the grid voltage orientation control (VOC) for gird-side converter and power control for BDBBC are applied. During the grid failures, it automatically switches to mode fault, where power control for GSC and voltage control for BDBBC are developed. Simulation results in MATLAB/SIMULINK verified the correctness and feasibility of the integrated control strategy.

Author Keywords: Permanent magnet synchronous generator based wind turbine generation system (PMSG-based WTGS)

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of resonance characteristics of MIDC systems based on ETAP
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Shanghai power grid is a multi-infeed AC/DC hybrid power systems with four inverter stations. Due to monitoring harmonics magnifying phenomenon about 11th order characteristic harmonic of HVDC (high voltage direct current) transmission system in Shanghai power grid , the resonance characteristics of Shanghai power grid is studied in this paper. Based on the parameters of 500kV and 220kV Shanghai power grid and equivalent loads of 220 kV lower voltage grades , the simulation model is built on the power system analysis software ETAP developed by OTI company in America. Scan the impedance-frequency characteristics of the Shanghai grid 500kV buses in different switching combination ways of AC filters. Frequency scan result shows series parallel resonance points of 500kV buses in Shanghai power grid and the influence of different switching combination ways on resonance points. At last, the measures to improve resonance characteristics of Shanghai power grid are proposed.

articleTitle: Voltage sag evaluation in unbalanced three-phase distribution network with distributed generations
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: This paper proposes a new algorithm to evaluate the voltage sag in unbalanced three-phase distribution network with distributed generations (DG). The paper models fault characteristics (fault line, location, type, duration, impedance) and DG output. By using two point estimation method (2PEM), the random probability problem in voltage sag simulation is transformed into multiple deterministic problems. Through computing the mean, the standard deviation and the third central moment of each node in distribution network, the probability density functions (PDF) of each node can be got based on Cornish-Fisher expansion (CFE) series, and then the voltage sag index System Average Root Mean Square Variation Frequency Index (SARFI) can be computed. Weak branches in distribution network are analyzed. Experiments have been made on the IEEE 13-bus test case with the consideration of two stochastic DG units. Thirteen scenarios simulations about voltage sag and comparison with Monte Carlo Simulation have been made. The comparisons with different wind turbine models have been provided. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for voltage sag evaluation have been proved.

articleTitle: A novel control strategy based on multi-agent for wind farm power dispatching
publicationTitle: International Conference on Renewable Power Generation (RPG 2015)
abstract: Nowadays, active power reference of wind farm from power grid dispatch center should be allocated to wind turbines.
